effect_mechanism: A global meta-analysis of silvopastoral systems against open pasture reports a pooled biodiversity log response ratio of 0.25 (a 28.4% difference), and the Colombian sustainable-ranching completion report attributes increased species richness and abundance, including many forest-dependent and endangered species, to silvopastoral systems at farm and landscape level [ev_biodiversity_outcome_nguyen26_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_cmscr20_8]. In the Colombian Amazon piedmont, silvopastoral projects significantly reduced deforestation rates compared with control properties, which enters as a forest-cover component [ev_landscape_forest_cover_bur24_2]. In Colombia, intensive silvopastoral systems held four times more birds and 35% higher bird species richness than grass monocultures, and ant species richness was 62% higher than in treeless pastures in the same landscape [ev_biodiversity_outcome_montagnini15_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_montagnini15_2].
conditionality: The comparator matters: the meta-analysis gain is against open pasture, and the same table reports negative log response ratios for silvopasture compared with native forest, so the benefit applies where trees are added to treeless pasture, not where silvopasture replaces forest [ev_biodiversity_outcome_nguyen26_1]. The envelope is adjacent to the LIC/LMIC target: the measured project outcome is from upper-middle-income Colombia and the meta-analysis carries no income-group tag, so transfer to low-income pastoral systems is not established by these units [ev_biodiversity_outcome_cmscr20_8, ev_biodiversity_outcome_nguyen26_1]. The Colombian bird and ant figures are earlier studies cited in a CATIE edited volume [ev_biodiversity_outcome_montagnini15_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_montagnini15_2].

effect_mechanism: Shade and timber trees in tree-crop systems add biomass carbon over the crop alone. Total biomass carbon in cocoa agroforestry, including cocoa and shade trees, is on average 2.5 times higher than in monoculture [ev_carbon_sequestration_niether20_1]. In Costa Rican coffee agroforestry, an eight-year eddy-covariance carbon balance of trees, coffee, litter and soil gave a mean storage of 3.6 t C/ha/yr, and shaded coffee plots held 29,8 Mg ha-1 more above-ground biomass carbon than full-sun plantations [ev_carbon_sequestration_seghieri19_5, ev_carbon_sequestration_villa20_6]. East African perennial tree-crop systems hold 29.9 Mg C ha−1 of above-ground carbon [ev_carbon_sequestration_muthuri23_4], and modelled Ethiopian enset-coffee and tree-coffee systems translate to biomass carbon of 139.5 and 153.4 Mg/ha [ev_carbon_sequestration_muthuri23_6]. A coffee review reports agroforestry can improve soil organic matter by 20–35% [ev_soil_organic_carbon_patil25_5].
conditionality: The soil side is weaker than the biomass side: the cocoa meta-analysis found no significant differences in soil chemical properties between agroforestry and monoculture [ev_soil_organic_carbon_niether20_1], and the coffee soil figure is a review's second-hand reading [ev_soil_organic_carbon_patil25_5]. The Costa Rican coffee units are from a high-income country, and the shaded-coffee figure is cited from earlier work [ev_carbon_sequestration_seghieri19_5, ev_carbon_sequestration_villa20_6]; the Ethiopian figures are model outputs cited second-hand [ev_carbon_sequestration_muthuri23_6]. The East African and Ethiopian figures are stocks, not annual rates [ev_carbon_sequestration_muthuri23_4]. Coffee, cocoa and enset units are crop-specific; the low- and lower-middle-income fit rests on the cocoa meta-analysis and the East African review [ev_carbon_sequestration_niether20_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_muthuri23_4].

effect_mechanism: In Sudano-Sahelian cropland, shrubs and trees on agricultural fields had an overall positive but variable effect on soil total carbon (+ 20 to 75%), and a cited meta-analysis reports that soil under Faidherbia albida canopy holds on average 46 per cent more organic carbon than outside it [ev_soil_organic_carbon_felix18_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_faosen24_1]. The externally audited Humbo FMNR project in Ethiopia reports CO2 sequestered since 2007 [ev_carbon_sequestration_wvfmnr19_11]. The Kenyan FMNR WOCAT compiler adds that increasing tree cover through FMNR is one of the ways to sequester carbon in biomass [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_507_2019_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases].
conditionality: Two literature units measure soil carbon under trees (a component of sequestration), and the Humbo figure is a project total from a World Vision self-evaluation with no per-hectare or per-year denominator [ev_soil_organic_carbon_felix18_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_faosen24_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_wvfmnr19_11]. The literature is from semi-arid West Africa and Ethiopia (low- and lower-middle-income countries) [ev_soil_organic_carbon_felix18_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_wvfmnr19_11]. The WOCAT unit is a compiler judgement on a documented technology sheet, not a measured stock or rate [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_507_2019_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases]. Measured directly on Ethiopian wheat farms, soil organic C did not differ significantly under and outside the Faidherbia albida canopy at the end of the 2013 cropping season, so the cited 46 per cent canopy gain was not reproduced at that site; this null lowers the agreement rather than the class [ev_soil_organic_carbon_sida18_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_faosen24_1].

effect_mechanism: In rainfed cropping, trees and shelterbelts cool the crop. Under Faidherbia albida parkland trees in Ethiopia, midday air temperature at wheat floral height was lowered by up to 6°C against the open field, peaking at 29oC under the canopy versus 36oC outside [ev_microclimate_buffering_sida18_1]. A meta-analysis of Chinese farmland found shelterbelts reduced summer air temperature by 4.01% against unsheltered fields [ev_microclimate_buffering_hao26_1], and a review reports, second-hand, that poplar alley cropping in Germany was 3.4°C cooler than sole wheat on hot summer days [ev_microclimate_buffering_dobhal24_4].
conditionality: The row carries a harm signal: an FAO review in Senegal states, second-hand, that windbreak hedges generally cause a slight rise in temperature in the protected plots, with impacts varying by crop and growth stage, so shelter designs that cut wind may warm rather than cool [ev_microclimate_buffering_faosen24_16]. The units measure air temperature, a component of heat-stress impact, not heat-stress yield losses [ev_microclimate_buffering_sida18_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_hao26_1]. They span low-income Ethiopia, lower-middle-income Senegal, upper-middle-income China and high-income Germany [ev_microclimate_buffering_sida18_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_faosen24_16, ev_microclimate_buffering_hao26_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_dobhal24_4].

effect_mechanism: In high-income settings, agroforestry has been found both to raise and to lower output. Gains: in subarctic Ontario, a site lined by willow windbreaks produced about 300 g/m2 of bean pods against about 60 g/m2 at an open site, and potato tuber yield was 33% greater (3200 versus 2400 g/m2) [ev_crop_yield_barbeau18_1, ev_crop_yield_barbeau18_2]; cited studies from Cañas, Costa Rica found milk production more than 15% higher for cows grazing silvopasture than in full sun and dry-season weight gains 2 to 5% higher on high tree-density pasture [ev_livestock_productivity_navas10_2, ev_livestock_productivity_navas10_3]; and a cited Costa Rican study found moderate shade gave coffee yields similar to, or 3% higher than, full sun [ev_crop_yield_villa20_4]. Losses: a cited Costa Rican experiment recorded a 30% coffee yield reduction in the shaded system against coffee monoculture [ev_crop_yield_dsantos23_11], and earlier work cited in a temperate alley-cropping study found greater crop yield losses near shelterbelts in dry years because of tree–crop competition [ev_crop_yield_majaura25_3].
conditionality: What separates the sides is the system and the competition for resources. The gains are livestock under tree cover and windbreak-sheltered vegetables in Ontario, where the plots were irrigated from ditches, whereas the losses are crops competing with trees: shelterbelt-edge cropping in dry years and established shade over coffee [ev_crop_yield_barbeau18_2, ev_crop_yield_majaura25_3, ev_crop_yield_dsantos23_11]. In Costa Rican coffee several units find no difference: a case study recorded no negative yield effect of shade, systems under 30 % shade cover did not differ in yield from full sun with management intensity driving yield instead, and young shaded coffee did not differ in fruiting nodes [ev_crop_yield_seghieri19_2, ev_crop_yield_villa20_3, ev_crop_yield_villa20_2]. All units are from high-income settings outside the LIC/LMIC target; most are earlier findings read second-hand through reviews, while the Ontario result was measured directly but at a single windbreak-lined site against a single open site [ev_livestock_productivity_navas10_2, ev_crop_yield_villa20_3, ev_crop_yield_barbeau18_1]. The coffee units are crop-specific [ev_crop_yield_villa20_4, ev_crop_yield_dsantos23_11].

effect_mechanism: Millet yields are reported to double or triple under Faidherbia albida in Senegal, a cited meta-analysis reports mean yield increases of 150 per cent for maize and 73 per cent for sorghum under its canopy, and millet and groundnut yields were higher in plots with intensive FMNR [ev_crop_yield_faosen24_8, ev_crop_yield_faosen24_9, ev_crop_yield_seghieri19_14]. On paired on-farm plots in Ethiopia, wheat under Faidherbia albida crowns yielded 23-26% more grain than open-field wheat in the normal seasons of 2013 and 2014, and up to 85% more in 2015, an El Niño year in which both yields were low; available N close to the crowns was 35-55% larger than under sole wheat [ev_crop_yield_sida18_1, ev_crop_yield_sida18_2, ev_soil_nitrogen_sida18_1]. Shrubs on Sudano-Sahelian fields often raised millet and sorghum yields (−25 to + 120%), and soil nitrogen was higher beneath shrubs and Faidherbia albida canopies, used here as a component [ev_crop_yield_felix18_1, ev_soil_nitrogen_felix18_1, ev_soil_nitrogen_faosen24_2]. In Maradi, Niger, millet yields rose by 120 to 209 kg/ha where FMNR was older than 6 years, with smaller increases for younger FMNR, and FMNR is estimated to have raised yields by an average of 100 kg/ha over 5 million hectares [ev_crop_yield_abasse23_1, ev_crop_yield_abasse23_3]. In Lempira, Honduras, the Quesungual system raised maize yields from 1.9 to 3.2 tonnes per hectare and bean yields from 0.8 to 2.0 tonnes per hectare, and its crops withstood the severe 1997 drought that caused losses for non-adopters [ev_crop_yield_chaudhury11_1, ev_crop_yield_chaudhury11_2, ev_crop_yield_chaudhury11_3]. Under Sahelian parkland trees, tuber yield is improved (+0.40 to +1.67 t ha-1) and legumes are less affected than cereals, and tree fodder is crucial in the dry season and during drought [ev_crop_yield_bayala14_1, ev_forage_productivity_bayala14_1].
conditionality: Groundnut under Faidherbia albida behaved variably and groundnut and millet yields fell under Cordyla pinnata, so the effect depends on which trees are retained [ev_crop_yield_faosen24_10, ev_crop_yield_faosen24_11]. The pooled magnitude draws on two soil-nitrogen percentages and an FMNR crop-value figure from a self-evaluation brief that calls results elsewhere mixed, and the Ghana figure is a share of households reporting higher yield [ev_soil_nitrogen_faosen24_2, ev_soil_nitrogen_felix18_1, ev_crop_yield_wvfmnr19_4, ev_crop_yield_talensi21_1]. Cereals often lose: in Maradi, FMNR did not significantly increase grain yields, the income gain being attributed to crop diversification instead, and under parkland trees cereal grain yield ranged from a loss of 0.54 t ha-1 under Balanites aegyptiaca to a gain of 0.24 t ha-1 under F. albida, with reductions attributed to competition for light, nutrients and water [ev_crop_yield_haglund11_1, ev_crop_yield_bayala14_1]. The Niger yield figures are earlier estimates cited in a grey-literature review, and the Honduran yields are before-and-after case-study figures for a slash-and-mulch system [ev_crop_yield_abasse23_1, ev_crop_yield_abasse23_3, ev_crop_yield_chaudhury11_1]. The Ethiopian drought-year gain stays separate from the normal-season gain; at the same site soil total N did not differ significantly under and outside the canopy at the end of the 2013 season despite the larger available N near the crowns, and the yield benefit of canopy cooling is modelled and appeared only with applied N [ev_crop_yield_sida18_1, ev_crop_yield_sida18_2, ev_soil_nitrogen_sida18_2, ev_crop_yield_sida18_3, ev_crop_yield_sida18_4].

effect_mechanism: Under silvopastoral systems in Colombia, mean erosion fell by 35.3 percent in the Coffee Ecoregion (12.3 t/ha a year against 19 t/ha on degraded pasture) and by 5.4 percent in the Cesar River Valley (17.5 against 18.5 t/ha) [ev_erosion_hazard_cmscr20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_cmscr20_2]. A Brazilian review explains that agroforestry increases soil cover and improves soil structure, protecting against raindrop impact and reducing wind speed and surface runoff [ev_erosion_hazard_santos25_2]. Runoff was higher on grass pasture than in tree-dominated fodder banks, so tree cover attenuates runoff and the soil erosion it causes [ev_runoff_reduction_cisneros24_1]. In Chiapas, Mexico, after Hurricane Stan, coffee farms with more complex vegetation suffered less landslide damage, the farm area hit by landslides rose as vegetation complexity fell, and roadside landslides were more numerous where complexity was lower [ev_erosion_hazard_philpott08_10, ev_erosion_hazard_philpott08_2, ev_erosion_hazard_philpott08_3]. In Misiones, Argentina, a cited study found the erosion and soil exhaustion of yerba mate monoculture much smaller when the crop is associated with trees [ev_erosion_hazard_montagnini15_1].
conditionality: The reduction differs widely between the Colombian regions, and the comparator is degraded pasture [ev_erosion_hazard_cmscr20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_cmscr20_2]. The evidence is from upper-middle-income Latin America, matching this scope row but not LIC/LMIC evidence, and the Brazilian unit is a review statement working through runoff, a component of erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_cmscr20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_cmscr20_2, ev_erosion_hazard_santos25_2]. The fodder-bank runoff comparison is a review citation without a size, and runoff is a component of erosion [ev_runoff_reduction_cisneros24_1]. The Chiapas evidence is crop-specific coffee from a single hurricane: the landslide-volume and landslide-size trends were only marginal (P = 0.062), and nearby forest cover did not influence landslide frequency or extent [ev_erosion_hazard_philpott08_3, ev_erosion_hazard_philpott08_5, ev_erosion_hazard_philpott08_4]. The yerba mate unit is read second-hand from a CATIE edited volume and gives no size [ev_erosion_hazard_montagnini15_1].

effect_mechanism: A sub-Saharan meta-analysis finds that agroforestry improved infiltration and soil moisture content compared to the control, with a weighted response ratio of 1.6 for soil moisture across 62 observations from 27 studies, and 70% of soil-moisture observations above RR 1 [ev_soil_water_retention_kuyah19_1]. Wetter soil under trees eases the crop's water stress. A cited statement adds that rainfall over agricultural land can shift with continental land cover, increasing with more upwind tree cover [ev_water_regulation_vannoordwijk21_4].
conditionality: The meta-analysis pools agroforestry practices without separating soil depth, so it cannot show whether trees and crops compete for deeper water; the Faidherbia parkland evidence that does show subsoil depletion sits in the regeneration-farmland row [ev_soil_water_retention_kuyah19_1]. The effect on infiltration was greater than that on soil moisture [ev_soil_water_retention_kuyah19_1]. The upwind-rainfall shift is a continental-scale effect from a secondary citation, not a field-scale one [ev_water_regulation_vannoordwijk21_4]. Groundwater-recharge findings are carried in the agroforestry catchment water yield rows.

effect_mechanism: Regenerated and retained trees on farmland compete with the crop for deeper soil water: under Faidherbia albida parkland in Ethiopia, soil moisture in the sub-soil was the least for wheat with tree, intermediate for sole tree and the highest for open field, while the authors observed no variation in topsoil moisture content between treatments [ev_soil_water_retention_sida18_1, ev_soil_water_retention_sida18_2]. That measured subsoil depletion is a harm to crop water supply for the adopter. The Kenyan FMNR WOCAT sheet points the other way, its compiler crediting an increase in water retention which increases the ground water levels [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_507_2019_water_availability].
conditionality: The direction is set by the measured Ethiopian study; the WOCAT unit is a compiler judgement on a documented technology sheet rather than a soil-moisture measurement and weighs little against it [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_507_2019_water_availability]. The rating and the measurement need not contradict: the rating speaks of groundwater, the measurement of subsoil water under a growing crop. The Ethiopian parkland trees were heavily pruned on farmers' fields; whether pruning or tree density changes the subsoil draw-down is not tested [ev_soil_water_retention_sida18_1]. The cited parkland tree-density result for groundwater recharge sits in the regeneration catchment water yield row.
